name: rtk
hint: condenses shell command output (git, tests, builds, ls) before the agent reads it
trims: Shell command output, at the source: a hook rewrites known commands (git, test runners, builds, grep, ls) to rtk, which drops noise and keeps errors.
helps: Long, noisy terminal output: test suites, builds, git logs, package managers. It never sees file reads, searches or MCP results, and an independent benchmark found little change in the billed cost on Claude, so treat it as cheap and low-risk rather than a big saver.
caveats: Installs a PreToolUse hook in each agent's global config. Another project named rtk exists; `rtk gain` must work.

guidance: Shell output is condensed by rtk before you read it. Treat it as the complete result and batch related commands into one call.
- Re-run a command as `rtk bypass <cmd>` only when its result is unusable: empty when output was clearly expected, contradicting its exit code, or garbled.
- A truncated result names its own recovery path (such as `rtk recall <hash>`); use that instead of re-running.
- Agents with an rtk hook (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Pi, Hermes) rewrite commands automatically. Elsewhere, prefix common commands yourself: `rtk git status`, `rtk test npm test`.
